existing.description: The International Research Training Program (iRTP) is the Australian Government's Research Training Program scholarship scheme for international graduate research students, administered by Macquarie University on behalf of the Department of Education. Successful PhD applicants receive a tuition fee offset for a maximum of three years plus a living allowance stipend of $40,900 per annum for up to three years and a travel concession on the local OPAL card. The award is open to international applicants commencing a full-time Master of Research or PhD at Macquarie in Session 1 2027, and those applying for an iRTP are automatically considered for the University-funded iMQRES. Applications for the 2027 round opened 15 June 2026 and closed 31 July 2026 at 11pm.
eligibility: Be a citizen of a country other than Australia or New Zealand and not an Australian permanent resident, at the time of application
Intend to reside in Sydney, Australia during candidature
Plan to undertake a Master of Research or Doctor of Philosophy full-time in Session 1 2027
Meet the admission criteria for the MRes or PhD and all criteria for admission to Macquarie University
Meet the English language requirement for a Macquarie research degree
Hold a valid visa enabling commencement of onshore study in Session 1 2027
Have completed their degree (applicants in the final semester of their current program are not eligible, except Macquarie applicants)
Have confirmation of supervision from an eligible Macquarie University researcher — compulsory for FOA, FMHHS and FSE, desirable for MQBS
existing.eligibility_summary: At the time of application applicants must be citizens of a country other than Australia or New Zealand, not Australian permanent residents, intend to reside in Sydney during candidature, plan to undertake a Master of Research or PhD full-time in Session 1 2027, meet admission and English language requirements, hold a visa enabling onshore commencement, have completed their prior degree, and have confirmation of supervision from an eligible Macquarie researcher.
benefits: Tuition fee offset for a maximum of three years
Living allowance stipend of $40,900 per annum for up to three years
Travel concession applied to the local transport OPAL card (PhD applicants)
coverage: Tuition fee offset for a maximum of three years (PhD)
Living allowance stipend of $40,900 per annum for up to three years
Travel concession applied to the local transport OPAL card (PhD applicants)
requirements: Select 'International Research Scholarship' as the scholarship type in the Macquarie graduate research application
Be enrolled or apply as a full-time MRes or PhD student for Session 1 2027
Lodge the application before the 31 July 2026 11pm deadline; incomplete applications are withdrawn and cannot be held over
documents: Confirmation of supervision from an eligible Macquarie University researcher
Evidence of English language proficiency meeting the Macquarie research degree requirement
Evidence of overseas qualifications for AQF comparability assessment
Full documentation of achievements to support assessment of qualifications
existing.english_requirement: Must meet the English language requirement for a Macquarie research degree.
application_method: Submit a Macquarie graduate research application and select 'International Research Scholarship' as the scholarship type
If already enrolled in a Macquarie graduate research program or holding a recent PhD letter of offer, submit a Scholarship Only online application instead
existing.selection_notes: Macquarie ranks applicants on academic merit, relevant research output and experience and/or potential, and alignment with the University's Research Strategy. Selection also considers the research environment, including project alignment with research strategy and priorities, the quality of the supervisory team, and the international standing of the research area. Outcomes for the 2027 round were due in early October 2026; applicants not notified by 15 November 2026 should consider the application unsuccessful.
existing.best_fit: International applicants with a completed degree, a Macquarie supervisor and a research proposal aligned with Macquarie's Research Strategy 2035, applying for a full-time MRes or PhD in Session 1 2027.
existing.notes: Applicants to the iRTP are automatically considered for the University-funded iMQRES in the same round. The number of international places funded through the RTP varies from year to year.
existing.duration: Up to three years for PhD applicants; MRes applicants may be counter-offered entry with a provisional three-year PhD
existing.application_period: Session 1 2027 international scholarship round: 15 June 2026 to 31 July 2026, 11pm.
existing.deadline_display: Applications open 15 June 2026, close 31 July 2026 at 11pm for Session 1 2027. The next round's dates are not yet published.
existing.program_type: Government-funded (Department of Education) international research training scholarship administered by the university

existing.description: The International Scientia Coursework Scholarship (PUCA1025) is offered by UNSW Sydney through the UNSW Scholarships for International Students round (PUCA1029) to international students commencing full-time on-campus undergraduate or postgraduate coursework study. Two award levels are published: a full tuition fee scholarship for the minimum duration of the program, or $20,000 per annum paid towards tuition fees for the same period. Applicants must already hold an unconditional offer of admission, or a conditional English package offer, by the scholarship deadline. Selection is based on academic merit, leadership skills, extra-curricular activities and reasons for studying at UNSW, with evidence required in the online application.
eligibility: Commence full-time study in a UNSW undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree program, excluding UNSW Online and UNSW Canberra
Have received an offer of admission into an eligible program for the round's term by the scholarship deadline

Hold an undergraduate or postgraduate Letter of Offer (unconditional), or an undergraduate or postgraduate Conditional English Package Offer (UEEC) with enrolment in the UNSW Institute of Languages and successful completion before commencing
existing.eligibility_summary: International students commencing full-time study in a UNSW undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree program on campus (excluding UNSW Online and UNSW Canberra) in the round's intake term, who hold an unconditional offer of admission or a conditional English package offer by the scholarship deadline and who apply through the PUCA1029 Scholarship Application Online portal.
benefits: Full tuition fee scholarship for the minimum duration of the program (Offer 1), or $20,000 per annum towards tuition fees (Offer 2)
coverage: Offer 1: full tuition fee scholarship paid directly towards tuition fees for the minimum duration of the program
Offer 2: $20,000 per annum paid directly towards tuition fees for the minimum duration of the program
requirements: Register an account in the Scholarship Application Online portal or log in and submit the PUCA1029 application
Provide evidence in the online application for each selection criterion; unanswered questions or claims without supporting documentation will not be assessed
Submit the application and all supporting documentation before the closing time, as late applications or supporting documentation will not be accepted
documents: Evidence supporting academic merit in the online application
Evidence supporting leadership skills (school, workplace or community)
Evidence supporting extra-curricular activities (sporting, cultural activities, volunteer or work experience)
A written statement of reasons for undertaking studies at UNSW
Conditional English Package Offer enrolment evidence if relying on a UEEC offer
existing.english_requirement: Applicants may hold either an unconditional Letter of Offer or a Conditional English Package Offer (UEEC); UEEC holders must be enrolled in the UNSW Institute of Languages and complete the program before commencing.
application_method: Register or log in to the Scholarship Application Online portal
Submit the UNSW Scholarships for International Students application for the round (PUCA1029)
Answer all selection-criterion questions and upload supporting documentation before the deadline
existing.selection_notes: Applicants are assessed on academic merit, leadership skills (school, workplace or community), extra-curricular activities (sporting, cultural activities, volunteer or work experience) and reasons for undertaking studies at UNSW. UNSW reserves the right not to award a scholarship where there is no applicant of sufficient merit or where eligibility and selection criteria are not met.
existing.best_fit: International applicants with an unconditional UNSW offer for an on-campus undergraduate or postgraduate coursework place in the round's intake term who can evidence academic merit, leadership and extra-curricular involvement.
existing.notes: Two award levels exist. Offer 1 is a full tuition fee scholarship; Offer 2 is $20,000 per annum towards tuition fees. Offers are made on the basis of the admission application's academic merit. UNSW College students and UAC International applicants expecting an admission offer after the scholarship deadline are recommended to apply before the deadline.
existing.duration: For the minimum duration of the program
existing.application_period: Term 2, 2026 international commencement round: 1 December 2025 to 26 February 2026, 11:59pm AEST. Rounds are term-based and repeat each intake.
existing.deadline_display: The PUCA1029 application "will open on 1 December 2025 and close at AEST 11:59PM on 26 February 2026". That round has closed; the next Term round's dates are not yet published.
existing.program_type: University tuition-fee scholarship for international coursework students
